moments.selftext: The UK’s @AISecurityInst (AISI) has published a report on their recent cybersecurity evaluation of Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. The models attempted to complete an assignment in a setup where their normal safeguards were removed and they were deliberately given internet access. AISI reports that the models “engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations”. We’re grateful to AISI for their leadership in the important discussion about how to evaluate increasingly capable AI agents. We’re working closely with them to gather more details of the incident as we conduct our own investigation. Gaining a clear picture of Claude’s understanding of its situation—by examining its reasoning transcripts and running our own analyses—will help us identify the causes of its behavior. The prompts in the evaluation did not impose any specific restrictions on how the internet should be used. This and the removal of safeguards meant that the models were tested under “deliberately permissive conditions” that are not representative of any of our production models. Note that there was no evidence here of an escape from a secure environment. AISI’s disclosure of the incident can be found here:

moments.title: 🇮🇷🇺🇸 Tucker and Darryl Cooper revisit the American strike that killed roughly 168 people at a girls' school in Minab on the war's first morning The Shajareh Tayyebeh elementary school was hit on February 28 while classes
moments.selftext: 🇮🇷🇺🇸 Tucker and Darryl Cooper revisit the American strike that killed roughly 168 people at a girls' school in Minab on the war's first morning The Shajareh Tayyebeh elementary school was hit on February 28 while classes were still in session, and most of the dead were girls between seven and twelve years old. Israel said its forces were not operating in the area. A preliminary US assessment concluded American forces were likely responsible, and Amnesty has called the strike unlawful and demanded accountability. Cooper walks through the part that keeps pulling Tucker back to it, that the site was struck again roughly 40 minutes later while people were digging through the rubble. What lands hardest is everything that followed. NO APOLOGY anyone remembers, no accountability. Cooper says it belongs on the front page of every history book. Tucker's take is blunter, that a country capable of shrugging at the deaths of its enemy's children has given up something it will not get back easily. He's right. Source: @tuckercarlson / Writer: Daniel, Val
